1→\section{Introduction}
     2→\label{sec:intro}
     3→
     4→Multi-modal satellite data fusion has emerged as a critical capability for earth observation, combining complementary sensor modalities to overcome single-sensor limitations. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) provides all-weather imaging through cloud-penetrating microwave signals, capturing surface geometry and moisture, while optical sensors offer rich spectral information enabling precise material discrimination \cite{clerici2017fusion, orynbaikyzy2020crop}. However, effectively fusing these heterogeneous modalities remains challenging due to fundamental differences in measurement physics, multi-resolution characteristics, and spatiotemporally varying data quality, with current fusion approaches facing critical limitations for operational deployment.
     5→
     6→\subsection{Challenges in Multi-Modal Multi-Resolution Fusion}
     7→
     8→Existing fusion strategies—\textit{early fusion} (concatenating raw sensor data) or \textit{late fusion} (combining independent predictions)—fail to capture cross-modal dependencies between heterogeneous sensor modalities \cite{yu2025stsnet}. Operational satellites exhibit inherent multi-resolution characteristics: Sentinel-1 GRDH (10m), Sentinel-2 (10-60m), and reference datasets at coarser resolutions \cite{hoppinen2024evaluating}. Models trained on coarse targets underutilize fine-scale inputs, while upscaling introduces artifacts. Real-world observations exhibit variable quality from atmospheric conditions, sensor calibration drift, and processing artifacts \cite{poussin2025snow}, with traditional approaches assuming uniform quality. Most methods lack uncertainty quantification essential for operational decision-making. Recent advances in deep learning \cite{dosovitskiy2020image, hong2021rethinking} offer opportunities: CNNs excel at spatial feature extraction but struggle with long-range dependencies \cite{zhu2017deep}; ViTs model global relationships via self-attention but face quadratic complexity; hybrid CNN-Transformer architectures \cite{yang2025enhanced, gao2024relating} synergistically combine local and global modeling but require adaptation to earth observation constraints.
     9→
    10→\subsection{Contributions}
    11→
    12→This work introduces \textbf{CrossFuse}, a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture for general-purpose multi-modal multi-resolution data fusion in remote sensing. Our approach addresses the identified challenges through three principal methodological innovations:
    13→
    14→\begin{enumerate}
    15→    \item \textbf{Multi-Resolution Processing Framework:} A training strategy that aggregates features to match coarse-resolution labels through learned snow-aware pooling and produces high-resolution predictions via guided disaggregation, enabling training on coarse reference data while generating fine-scale outputs.
    16→
    17→    \item \textbf{Cross-Modal Attention Fusion:} Explicit modeling of bidirectional dependencies through multi-head cross-attention mechanisms. Query-key-value transformations capture inter-sensor relationships and enable adaptive modality weighting based on local scene characteristics and data quality.
    18→
    19→    \item \textbf{Quality-Aware Learning Framework:} Integration of multi-source quality metadata (cloud masks, atmospheric parameters, sensor quality flags) through adaptive loss weighting and curriculum learning with well-calibrated uncertainty estimates.
    20→\end{enumerate}
    21→
    22→The integrated architecture combines dual-path CNN backbones with attention mechanisms (CBAM for SAR, ECA for optical), cross-attention fusion, and spatial transformers (6 layers, 8 heads, 512-dim). On 18,117 test patches from 4 tiles, CrossFuse achieves 13.77\% MAE (38.7\% better than best baseline), 94.66\% accuracy, and 78.71\% F1-score. Statistical analysis confirms excellent calibration: $r=0.784$ ($p<0.001$), $R^2=0.588$, and Moran's I=$0.353$ ($p<0.001$), substantially exceeding baselines (CNN-Only: $r=0.525$, $R^2=0.239$). Ablation studies validate that hybrid CNN-Transformer design with cross-modal attention significantly outperforms alternatives.
    23→
    24→\subsection{Paper Organization}
    25→
    26→Section~\ref{sec:related_work} reviews related work in multi-modal fusion and deep learning architectures. Section~\ref{sec:proposed_method} presents our methodology with mathematical formulations. Section~\ref{sec:experiments} describes experimental setup and results including ablation studies. Section~\ref{sec:conclusion} concludes with contributions and future directions.
    27→
